report.tagline: The world's main search engine, now answering many questions with AI written answers (AI Overviews and AI Mode) while still earning most of its money from ads.
report.simpleSummary: Google Search is where most people type a question. For years it showed ten blue links and some ads. Now, for many questions, it shows an AI written answer at the top (AI Overviews), and you can switch to AI Mode to chat with it, ask follow-ups, or search with your camera or voice. Google earns money when people click the ads shown next to results and inside these AI answers. The big question is whether AI answers make as much ad money as the old links.

overview.whatItDoes: Google Search finds information on the web and now often writes the answer itself using Gemini models. AI Overviews appear on top of normal results; AI Mode is a full chat-style search tab where you can ask long, multi-part questions. Search is free; advertisers pay when users click their ads.
howItWorks: A user types, speaks or points the camera (Google Lens) at something.
Google's index of the web and its Gemini model build an AI answer with links to sources.
Ads appear above results, in Shopping listings and now inside AI Overviews and AI Mode.
Advertisers bid in an auction for keywords; Google charges only when someone clicks (cost per click).
Queries in AI Mode are about 3 times longer than normal searches, and 1 in 5 uses voice, images or documents.
Google pays partners like Apple and Samsung to be the default search engine on their devices.
overview.valueProposition: For users: fast, free answers to almost any question, now with explanations instead of a list of links. For advertisers: reaching people at the exact moment they are looking for something.

businessModel.summary: Google Search is free for users and makes money from advertisers. Advertisers bid in auctions and pay when people click. Search and other revenue was $63 billion in one quarter, the largest part of Alphabet. AI answers cost more to produce and so far earn less per query, which is the core tension.

revenueStreams.stream: Ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode

Paid plans with more powerful AI features; small next to ads.

businessModel.pricing: Free for users. Advertisers pay per click through auctions; prices vary by keyword from a few rupees to thousands of rupees for competitive terms like insurance.
costDrivers: Computing cost of running AI answers, higher than plain links
Payments to Apple, Samsung and others for default placement
businessModel.unitEconomics: Suppose Google handles 1,000 normal searches. Ads are clicked on some of them and Google might earn roughly $20 to $50 from those 1,000 searches in the US, at a cost of under a cent per search to serve. An AI Mode answer costs several times more in computing, and Google said AI Mode queries currently earn less money than normal search. So each switch from links to AI answers adds cost and, for now, loses some revenue per query. Google is betting longer queries and better ad formats will close that gap.

growth.moat: Search has a huge data and distribution moat: billions of searches a day teach Google what people want, and it is the default on most phones and browsers. AI chatbots threaten the habit, but Google's index, Gemini models, and its own chips let it build AI answers at lower cost than most rivals.

pmLessons: Disrupting yourself is hard when the old product makes huge money; Google must move to AI answers while protecting ads.
Watch the whole ecosystem: if publishers stop getting traffic, the content that feeds the product suffers.
New behaviour, like longer questions, can open new uses, but you must find a way to earn from them.
Distribution, like being the default, is a product advantage that rivals struggle to match.

interviewQuestions.question: How would you monetise AI Mode without hurting user trust?
interviewQuestions.hint: Ads that fit the question, clear labels, guardrails on sensitive topics, test formats, track revenue per query and satisfaction.

interviewQuestions.question: Search revenue growth slowed. How do you diagnose it?
interviewQuestions.hint: Split into queries, paid clicks and CPC; by region, device and AI vs non-AI queries. Google itself cited currency, EU rules and AI Mode.

interviewQuestions.question: What is the north star metric for Google Search in the AI era?
interviewQuestions.hint: Successful answers per day. Why not clicks: AI answers reduce clicks. Add guardrails like publisher clicks.

interviewQuestions.question: Design AI Mode for first-time internet users in India.
interviewQuestions.hint: Voice first, local languages, low data use, simple follow-ups. Measure weekly active users and re-query rate.

interviewQuestions.question: How should Google respond to ChatGPT?
interviewQuestions.hint: Strengths (index, distribution, cost), weaknesses (habit among young users). Options: AI Mode by default, Gemini app, partnerships.
